    StartersTiana's beignetsFried yeast dough squares, soft and puffyHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast50g caster sugar2 eggs50g butter, melted250ml evaporated milk125ml warm water1 L vegetable oil, for frying100g icing sugarMix the flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, butter and evaporated milk with enough warm water to a soft dough.Knead briefly until smooth.Cover and prove until doubled.Roll out and cut into squares.Fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C in batches until puffed and golden.Bury under icing sugar and serve hot.Muffuletta cob loaf sandwichCob loaf layered with olive salad, salami, ham and provoloneHow to make it1 cob loaf150g salami150g leg ham150g provolone200g green olives100g giardinieraChop the olives and giardiniera together for an olive salad.Hollow the loaf slightly.Layer with olive salad, salami, ham and provolone, then more olive salad.Wrap tightly and press under a heavy weight overnight in the fridge.Cut into small wedges.Bayou crab cakes with Creole remouladeLouis, Ray and the frogs in the bayouHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crab cakes bound with mayo, mustard and spring onion, fried crisp, with a punchy Creole remoulade of pickles, capers and hot sauce.Mix 400g drained crab meat with 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 2 sliced spring onions, 1 egg, 60g panko and 1/2 tsp Cajun spice.Shape into 8 cakes and chill 30 minutes.Fry in oil and butter for 3 minutes a side until golden.For the remoulade, mix 120g mayo with 1 tbsp chopped pickles, 1 tbsp capers, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tsp hot sauce and paprika.Serve with lemon.Fried okra with hot pepper vinegarMama Odie says dig a little deeper.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsTiana's Palace shrimp and gritsGarlic bacon prawns over cheddar polentaHow to make it200g polenta1 L water150g cheddar, grated150g bacon, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed500g green prawns, peeled2 tsp Cajun seasoning3 spring onions, slicedPeel the prawns and prepare the spring onions.Simmer the polenta in the water, stirring, until thick.Beat the cheddar into the polenta.Fry the bacon until crisp.Add the garlic, prawns and Cajun seasoning and cook until the prawns are pink.Spoon over the polenta and scatter with spring onion.Daddy James's chicken and sausage gumboThe gumbo Tiana's daddy taught her, shared with the whole streetHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken and smoky sausage in a dark, nutty roux with okra, capsicum, celery and onion, ladled over rice with spring onion and hot sauce.Stir 80ml oil and 80g plain flour in a heavy pot over medium heat for 20 minutes until dark brown.Add 1 diced onion, 1 green capsicum and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes.Add 600g diced chicken thighs, 300g sliced smoked sausage, 2 tsp Cajun spice and 1.2L chicken stock.Simmer for 1 hour, adding 200g sliced okra for the last 15 minutes.Serve over 300g cooked rice with spring onion and hot sauce.SweetsTiana's Palace bananas fosterBananas cooked in butter, brown sugar and cinnamonHow to make it50g pecans, chopped60g butter100g brown sugar1/2 tsp ground cinnamon4 bananas1 orange1 tsp vanilla extract500ml vanilla ice creamToast the pecans in a dry pan.Melt the butter in a frying pan with the brown sugar and cinnamon and stir until bubbling.Add the bananas, halved lengthways and across, and cook until caramelised on each side.Pour in the orange juice and vanilla and let it bubble into a glossy sauce.Spoon over scoops of ice cream and scatter with the pecans.DrinksIced chicory coffee with milkStrong chicory coffee over ice with vanilla syrup and milkHow to make it4 tbsp ground coffee1 tbsp roasted chicory500ml boiling water60g caster sugar60ml water1 tsp vanilla extract600ml milk4 cups iceBrew the coffee with the chicory in the boiling water.Cool the coffee.Simmer the sugar, water and vanilla to a syrup.Fill glasses with ice, add syrup and cold milk, then pour over the coffee. For the kids, use decaf or just milk and syrup.
